findings.finding: Root license and package metadata disagree. The separate Aseprite submodule has not been fetched or audited.

evidence.observation: tools/aseprite-mcp references a separate Git repository

findings.impact: The framework license cannot be represented as consistent metadata, and the root license does not establish permissions for separately sourced software.
findings.change: Preserve the root MIT notice and pin the inspected commit; record the ISC discrepancy. Exclude submodules and packaged binaries from the resource pack.
findings.acceptance: Integration lock lists upstream commit, MIT notice hash, package metadata discrepancy, and zero included submodule paths.

findings.finding: Ordinary dependency installation executes a prepare lifecycle hook that changes repository hook configuration and index modes.

evidence.observation: sets local core.hooksPath .githooks and calls git update-index --chmod=+x

findings.impact: Importing the framework as a dependency can alter host repository behavior beyond selected role resources.
findings.change: Do not run its prepare hook in the destination repository. Any future dependency installation must use ignore-scripts in an isolated source checkout; copy only explicitly selected text resources.
findings.acceptance: Host core.hooksPath and index modes unchanged after integration; project contains no generated upstream hook installation.

findings.finding: Art integration merges an enabled Aseprite MCP server; root configuration also defines plugin hooks and unpinned optional servers.

evidence.observation: art module carries MCP configuration, mirrored in .agents/modules/art
aseprite local server lacks enabled:false; Godot command uses npx @coding-solo/godot-mcp; three local plugin hooks are listed
add merges module MCP fragment into selected harness configuration

findings.impact: Using the stock installer can activate an unreviewed runtime or override host configuration while the user only expects game team resources.
findings.change: Import selected module text as project-scoped references. Keep MCP integration as an explicit capability mapping to existing approved creative operations; do not copy root opencode.json, plugins, MCP fragments or AGENTS.md over the host project.
findings.acceptance: Selected-resource receipt excludes executable plugins and MCP configuration. Existing host MCP files are byte-identical before and after resource import.

findings.finding: Installer exit status alone does not prove successful module installation or validation.

evidence.observation: cmdAdd catches errors without assigning process.exitCode; runValidation prints WARN on nonzero child status
malformed MCP fragment test explicitly expects process exit status 0

findings.impact: A pipeline could publish partial or failed integration while reporting success.
findings.change: Use a purpose-built resource synchronizer with fail-closed validation, exact allowlist and content hashes. Invoke upstream standalone validator independently and check its process status.
findings.acceptance: Missing source, wrong commit, hash mismatch, unsafe path or pre-existing altered target each fails nonzero; valid selected-resource sync succeeds with complete receipt.

findings.finding: Agent definition conversion is not native authorization or runtime budget enforcement.

evidence.observation: Codex transform emits name, description and developer_instructions but does not enforce source maxTurns or tools fields
Employee assignment and skill references grant no execution scope; current native creative.execute authorization is checked per run

findings.impact: Registering imported agent definitions as permanent employees or permissions would silently change Donna authority and make declarative budgets appear enforceable.
findings.change: Map resources to existing engineering, design/graphics and QA roles; preserve employee IDs, owner authority and grant checks. Define panel roles as bounded task packets, not new privileged identities.
findings.acceptance: No native employee, owner, department, role or grant records are mutated by integration. All executable operations continue through the existing approved creative-tools contract.

findings.finding: Upstream structural validation passes, but it is not an end-to-end engine, provider, asset-rights or accuracy test.

evidence.observation: Tests harness transformations and configuration behavior with disposable fixtures

findings.impact: A passing framework suite cannot support a claim that Blender, Godot, Unreal, Aseprite or an AI provider is connected and production-ready.
findings.change: Report structural tests separately from local software probes, asset imports and render/export tests. Keep Unreal and Adobe declared unavailable/licensed until actual installation and access are verified.
findings.acceptance: Capability table distinguishes installed/probed, configured-only, reference-only, unavailable and externally licensed; no blanket complete-setup claim.

findings.finding: Generic art and game skills do not establish monument accuracy or source usage rights.

evidence.observation: Focuses on art bible, asset specifications, naming, format and performance budgets
Actual site assets have incomplete scale/control, detail coverage and/or license provenance constraints

findings.impact: A successful mesh import or attractive render could be mistaken for a survey-accurate reconstruction.
findings.change: Add host-project acceptance around source provenance, creator license, capture limitations, source units, coverage, vertex/face counts and measured export quality. Never generate missing ornament and label it observed.
findings.acceptance: Each site manifest separates observed captured geometry from modeled additions, retains source units unless calibrated, and blocks commercial-ready or survey-accurate labels without supporting evidence.

findings.finding: Stock recursive copy follows stat-resolved paths and allows broad force replacement; it is unnecessary for a read-only selected-resource integration.

evidence.observation: Recursive copy uses statSync, supports force overwrite, and installs dependency-missing modules after warnings

findings.impact: Blind reuse increases accidental overwrite and path/symlink risks, especially across existing project instructions.
findings.change: Use fixed module identifiers; reject symlinks and path traversal; permit only enumerated regular text files; stage to a temporary directory and publish only after hash/size checks. Existing modifications require a deliberate reviewed update.
findings.acceptance: Boundary tests cover symlink, traversal, changed existing file, missing required module dependency and interrupted staging without partial publication.
